meta.title: Billed compute for one event: all on AgentCore vs the split

spans.name: All on AgentCore: every event
spans.detail: Each tenant's microVM runs the whole agent loop and bills memory until its 5-minute idle timeout ends.

spans.name: Idle, 1 GB still billed
spans.detail: Runtime v2 reclaims idle memory after 120 seconds.

spans.name: Idle at the 128 MB floor
spans.detail: Billing stops when the 300-second idle timeout ends the session.

spans.name: Split, routine event (9 in 10)
spans.detail: The shared worker answers with the model and Gateway tools. No microVM starts, and billing stops when the turn ends.

spans.name: Split, code event (1 in 10)
spans.detail: Only these events start a microVM: the tenant's runtime session runs one script, then idles to its timeout.

spans.name: Worker turn, waits for the script
spans.detail: 5 seconds of agent loop plus about 30 seconds waiting for the runtime. The illustrative estimate counts only the 5 seconds.

cards.title: Why the split costs less
items: A microVM bills for its idle timeout after every event it serves
All on AgentCore, every event opens that window: 4,320 a month per tenant
In the split only code events do, about 432 a month; routine events pay seconds of shared Lambda

cards.title: Per tenant per month, illustrative estimate
items: Same in both: Nova Lite $0.83, Gateway and state $0.12

cards.title: Corrections the estimate does not make
items: Count each 30 s script in both designs: $4.24 all on AgentCore, $1.84 split
Add this repo's isolation boundary to the split: $1.99

cards.title: Measured on the sandbox, 19 Oct 2026
items: Worker turns averaged 4.2 s billed over 33 runs, against 5 s assumed
Turns that used only Gateway tools started no runtime
The idle runtime kept about 1 GB until the timeout, not 128 MB after 2 minutes
